content.overview: Section 36 of the Arbitration and Conciliation Act, 1996 is the enforcement provision. Where the time for making a s. 34 application has expired, the award is enforced in accordance with the Code of Civil Procedure, 1908 as if it were a decree of the court. Filing a s. 34 application does not by itself render the award unenforceable. A stay requires a separate application under s. 36(3). The court may grant a stay subject to such conditions as it deems fit, and for a money award it shall have due regard to the Code of Civil Procedure provisions for stay of a money decree. The 2021 proviso requires an unconditional stay pending the s. 34 application where the court is satisfied that the arbitration agreement or contract which is the basis of the award, or the making of the award, was induced or effected by fraud or corruption.
content.study: Keep the existing point: ask for a stay under s. 36(3) with the conditions the court imposes, often a deposit. Do not treat a s. 34 filing as a stay application. Add the fraud or corruption unconditional-stay proviso as a distinct condition, not as an automatic stay in every challenge.

learningObjectives: State when an award becomes enforceable under s. 36.
Apply the separate stay application and conditions in s. 36(3).
Isolate the unconditional-stay proviso for fraud or corruption.
enhancement.definition: Section 36 enforces an award like a CPC decree once the s. 34 period has expired, and it requires a separate, conditioned stay application if a set-aside application is pending.
enhancement.legalPrinciple: A challenge is not a stay. Enforcement is the default after the set-aside window, and a stay is discretionary and conditional except where the statutory fraud or corruption proviso applies.
enhancement.statutoryFramework: Arbitration and Conciliation Act, 1996, s. 36; CPC 1908 enforcement and money-decree stay provisions; set-aside application in s. 34; 2021 unconditional-stay proviso for fraud or corruption.
essentialIngredients: Time for s. 34 expired, or stay sought while a s. 34 application is pending
Enforcement as a decree under the CPC
Conditions, with due regard to CPC money-decree stay rules for a money award
Unconditional stay only if the court is satisfied of fraud or corruption in the agreement, contract, or making of the award
enhancement.detailedExplanation: The post-2015 structure removed the old automatic stay on the mere filing of a s. 34 petition. Section 36(1) treats the award as a decree for CPC enforcement once the set-aside period has expired. Section 36(2) says that filing a s. 34 application does not by itself make the award unenforceable, unless a stay is granted. Section 36(3) requires a separate application and allows conditions. For a money award the court looks to the CPC money-decree stay provisions. The proviso, as amended in 2021, is narrower than a general stay: unconditional stay pending disposal of the challenge is required where the court is satisfied that the arbitration agreement or the underlying contract, or the making of the award, was induced or effected by fraud or corruption. A deposit condition in an ordinary money-award stay is not the same as that unconditional stay.
examples: No s. 34 application is filed within time; the award-holder seeks execution as a decree.
A s. 34 petition is filed with no stay application; enforcement can proceed.
A money award is challenged and the court stays execution on a deposit condition, having regard to CPC money-decree stay practice.
The court is satisfied that the making of the award was effected by fraud; the unconditional-stay proviso is the provision to apply.
enhancement.problemApplication: Check whether the s. 34 window has expired; if a challenge is pending, look for a separate s. 36(3) application; classify the award as money or not; plead fraud or corruption only with facts that can satisfy the proviso. Do not equate filing with stay.
distinctions: Enforcement under s. 36 vs set-aside under s. 34
Filing a challenge vs an order staying the award
Conditional stay vs unconditional stay for fraud or corruption
Award enforced as a decree vs a Lok Adalat deemed decree

keyTakeaways: Expiry of the s. 34 period makes the award enforceable as a CPC decree.
A s. 34 filing is not itself a stay.
Stay needs a separate application and may be conditional.
Unconditional stay is tied to the fraud or corruption proviso.
